fixes.explanation: Elders aren't mentioned in this verse. Moses says, “Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded…” So the call is for skilled hands. Put me in front of a block of wood and a chisel, and you'd end up with a very sad pile of sawdust.

True, friend. The verse says everyone “…whose heart stirred him and whose spirit prompted him came and brought an offering to the LORD…” That happens after the congregation withdraws from Moses (Exodus 35:20-21). The people leave the meeting, and the gifts start coming. Now that's a meeting with a very good ending.

That's right. The men and women bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” Rings and necklaces are on that list. They present all of their gold as a wave offering to the LORD.

Cups and bowls aren't in this verse. The people bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” So the list is jewelry, from brooches to necklaces. Gold cups and bowls just aren't on it.

No crowns or shields in this verse, friend. It lists “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” The gifts named here are jewelry. Crowns and shields don't make the list.

Lead sounds reasonable, but it's not the word. The verse says the LORD gave both Bezalel and Oholiab “…the ability to teach others.” Bezalel is from the tribe of Judah, and Oholiab son of Ahisamach is from the tribe of Dan (Exodus 35:30, 34). Teaching is the gift named here. Good teachers do lead, I'll give you that.

New moons aren't in this verse. The text says the people “…continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning…” That's a lot more often than once a month. Those hearts kept stirring, day after day.
The text doesn't mention any tribal leaders in this scene. The craftsmen leave their work and say their words to Moses. The news goes to him, and that's the whole trip.

More workers isn't what they ask for. The craftsmen leave their work and tell Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do” (Exodus 36:5). So their report is about the gifts, not a need for help. If I were in that spot, I'd have asked for a nap.

Not quite, friend. The craftsmen say, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.” The words are more than enough, not exactly enough. This one is False.
